_format: skill-creator eval format. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions. expect_trigger false marks a should-not-trigger probe.

evals.prompt: Our CLAUDE.md is 500 lines and AGENTS.md is a slightly different copy of it. Claude keeps ignoring half of it. Clean this up properly.
assertions: Measures before editing (runs scripts/measure.py or reports line/byte counts and the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md relation)
Produces an inventory that assigns each section a destination: keep, docs/, hook or CI, skill, path rule, or delete
Makes AGENTS.md the canonical file and reduces CLAUDE.md to an @AGENTS.md import on its first line instead of a symlink or second copy
Moves knowledge into docs/ with a pointer row rather than deleting it outright
Proposes turning at least one must-always-hold rule into a hook, linter or CI check instead of prose

evals.prompt: Every time someone runs composer install, php artisan boost:install rewrites AGENTS.md and our hand-written project rules disappear. How do we stop losing them?
assertions: Explains that everything inside the laravel-boost-guidelines block is regenerated and hand-written text there is lost
Moves standing instructions to .ai/guidelines and project knowledge to docs/
Mentions the .gitignore pattern .ai/* with !.ai/guidelines/ when .ai is ignored
Proposes a CI check that regenerates and fails on any diff, using the same flags as the automatic run

evals.prompt: I put my own company's conventions in ~/.claude/rules, but now they show up when I work in a client's repo and contradict their rules. How should I set this up?
assertions: States that ~/.claude/rules and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md load in every project and that conflicting levels are resolved arbitrarily
Recommends scoping the company rules by an ancestor-directory CLAUDE.md (or a plugin/managed route for a team) instead of user-level rules
Suggests verifying in a fresh session in both a company repo and a client repo

evals.prompt: Set up the agent instructions for this repo. The team uses Claude Code, Cursor and opencode, and we want to try OpenHands.
assertions: Creates AGENTS.md as the canonical file and CLAUDE.md containing @AGENTS.md
Leads with commands the agent cannot guess (install, test, lint with flags) rather than an architecture overview
Places skills in .agents/skills with .claude/skills as a symlink to it
Keeps AGENTS.md well under 32 KiB and under roughly 200 lines

evals.prompt: Write a README for this repository that explains to new developers what the project does and how to run it.
assertions: Writes a README without treating it as an agent instruction file

evals.prompt: Write a new Claude skill that formats our changelog entries.
assertions: Treats the task as skill authoring, not as editing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
